**Starts** once #141 is merged.

## Why

Joe tests the coordinator by hand as it's built. Rating a turn, or a whole chat, with a note, right when it happens, records what went well and what went wrong while it's fresh. Later, the ratings get sorted into kinds of failure. The kinds that keep coming back become agent evaluations (#53). Phoenix can also turn rated spans into a dataset, which is what its experiments run on.

Phoenix's own UI can already rate a trace, but that means finding the turn in Phoenix later. From the chat, it's one click. Links from the chat to each turn's trace, and to the session, let Joe go from what he sees in the chat to how the coordinator got there. They take the place of the raw view, which #141 removes.

An **annotation** is a rating that Phoenix keeps on a span or a session: a name, a label, a score, a note, and who made it. A **session** in Phoenix groups a chat's turns by their `session.id`. That's the **agent session ID**, the Agent SDK's ID for the conversation (`agentSessionId` in `src/persistence/session.ts`), not the app's own session ID, which the page uses (systems design section 10).

## Design

- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 10.1 (the chat view).
- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), sections 4 (what the stream sends the browser) and 10 (traces, and how Phoenix is reached).
- Phoenix 20.26.0's source, at the [`arize-phoenix-v20.26.0`](https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix/tree/arize-phoenix-v20.26.0) tag: the redirect links in `js/app/src/Routes.tsx`, and the annotation routes in `src/phoenix/server/api/routers/v1/spans.py`, `sessions.py`, and `annotations.py`. Through the tunnel, Phoenix's own API docs are at `http://127.0.0.1:6006/docs`.

Agreed in chat on 2026-10-26:

- **Each reply gets a thumbs up and a thumbs down, and so does the whole session.** Either one opens a box for a note. Good turns get rated as well as bad ones.
- **Each reply gets a "View trace" link, and the chat gets a "View session" link.** Each opens Phoenix in a new tab. Phoenix 20.26 has redirect links that take our own IDs, so the app doesn't look anything up in Phoenix. `/redirects/spans/<span ID>` opens the trace with that span picked, so a turn's link needs only its turn span's ID. `/redirects/sessions/<session ID>` opens the session, and takes the agent session ID.
- **The browser never talks to Phoenix.** On the server, the browser can't reach it. So the page sends a rating to the app, under `/api`, and the app posts it to Phoenix, the way it sends traces. It posts with `fetch`, like the health check in `src/tracing/phoenix.ts`, not with a new package.
- **The links work only on Joe's machine, with the SSH tunnel up** (DEVELOPMENT.md section 2), since Phoenix's UI is at `http://127.0.0.1:6006` there and nowhere else.

What Phoenix 20.26 offers, from its source:

- `POST /v1/span_annotations` and `POST /v1/session_annotations` save annotations. Each one has a `name`, an `annotator_kind` of `HUMAN`, `CODE`, or `LLM`, a `result` with a `label`, a `score`, and an `explanation`, `metadata`, and an `identifier`.
- When an annotation with the same name and `identifier` is already there, Phoenix updates it in place of adding one.
- By default, Phoenix queues an annotation and replies at once. An annotation for a span or session it doesn't have yet is tried again every 10 seconds, up to 60 times, and then dropped with no error (`src/phoenix/db/insertion/span_annotation.py`, `session_annotation.py`, and `constants.py`). With `?sync=true`, it saves it before replying, and refuses one for a span it doesn't have, with a 404.
- The `/redirects/...` links aren't server redirects. Phoenix replies with its web page, and the page's own code asks Phoenix's GraphQL API which trace or session the ID belongs to (`getSpanByOtelId` and `getProjectSessionById`, in `js/app/src/pages/redirects/`). Then it moves the browser there.

## Open questions

- ~~What does a rating hold? A first guess is the name `rating`, the label `up` or `down`, the score 1 or 0, the note as the explanation, and `annotator_kind` `HUMAN`.~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: as guessed. The name is `rating` for both turns and sessions, the label `up` or `down`, the score 1 or 0, the note as the explanation (left out when there's none), and `annotator_kind` `HUMAN`. Systems design section 10.
- ~~Can a rating be changed, such as from up to down? If so, the `identifier` could be the user's ID, so each user has one rating per turn and per session.~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: yes. The `identifier` is the rater's user ID, so a new rating replaces that user's earlier one on the same turn or session. A rating can be flipped, not taken back. Functional spec 10.1, systems design section 10.
- ~~Who sees the trace and session links? Only Joe can open them. The app has no way to tell Joe from other users. One choice is to show them to everyone. Another is an environment value with Joe's user ID, which the page would learn through `/api/me` (`src/shared/me.schema.ts`).~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: everyone. For anyone else, they're dead links, which is harmless. The span ID and agent session ID aren't secret. Functional spec 10.1.
- ~~Who can rate? If any signed-in user can, the route checks that the user owns the session, as other session routes do (`src/api/owned.ts`). It can't check that a span ID belongs to that session, unless it asks Phoenix.~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: any signed-in user, on a session they own. The route checks ownership with `ownedSession()`, and that a span ID is 16 hex characters. It doesn't check that the span belongs to the session. For a session rating, the page sends no ID, and the server finds the agent session ID itself. Systems design section 4.
- ~~What happens when a rating comes before the turn's span reaches Phoenix? Spans are sent in batches every few seconds, and the turn span ends only after the reply does. With `sync=true`, Phoenix refuses it with a 404. Without it, check whether Phoenix keeps a queued annotation for a span it doesn't have yet. On a new chat's first turn, the session may not be in Phoenix yet either.~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: post without `sync=true`, and let Phoenix's queue cover the delay (see "What Phoenix 20.26 offers" above). The app adds no retry or wait. A rating on a span that never reaches Phoenix is dropped after about 10 minutes, with no error. If the app can't reach Phoenix, the page says the rating wasn't saved. The local check confirms a rating sent at once is kept. Systems design section 10.
- ~~Which turns can be rated and linked? The page gets a turn's span ID only for turns it streamed. A resumed session's earlier turns come from the transcript, which has no span IDs. So do turns the page shows after waiting on a turn that was already running when it loaded (`turnRunning` in `web/src/chat-state.ts`). A turn whose SDK call threw has no span ID either. The session's rating and link need only the agent session ID, which the server always has, so they work in every case.~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: only turns the page streamed. Turns loaded from the transcript get no thumbs and no link. They can be rated in Phoenix's own UI, from the session link. A turn whose SDK call threw does get a span ID, since the turn span is made before the SDK call, and the span ID is the turn's first event. The session's thumbs and link show once the session exists. Functional spec 10.1.
- ~~Where do the thumbs go on a failed turn with no reply? Failed turns are the ones most worth rating down.~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: each streamed turn gets a row under its last card, with the thumbs and "View trace". With no reply, that's under the user's message. A failed turn's row also says "The reply didn't finish.", so it still makes sense once the page's error line is gone. Functional spec 10.1.
- ~~Where does the page get Phoenix's address for the links? It could be written into the page as `http://127.0.0.1:6006`, or come from a `VITE_` value in `web/src/web-env.schema.ts`. The app's `PHOENIX_URL` won't do, since on the server it's `http://phoenix:6006`.~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: a constant in the page's code, since the browser reaches Phoenix through the tunnel at the same address, locally and on the live site. Systems design section 10.

## Do

- **Send each turn's span ID to the browser,** as the turn's first event, before the SDK call. `TurnTrace` (`src/agent/turn-trace.ts`) keeps the turn span private, and it's created in `runTurnWithSdk` (`src/agent/coordinator.ts`), so this means a way to read the span ID from it, and a change to `TurnEvent` (`src/agent/turn-event.ts`). Update the fake turn runner (`src/agent/run-turn.fake.ts`), `npm run chat`'s event printer (`src/chat.ts`), and `chatEventOf()` (`src/api/turn-stream.ts`) to match.
- **Send the page the agent session ID,** for the session link. Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: add it to the `session` event and to the resume reply (`SessionResponse` in `src/shared/session.schema.ts`), next to the app's session ID. A link can't go through the app to look it up, since a link click doesn't carry the sign-in token. The session rating route looks it up on the server.
- **Add an `/api` route that saves a rating** for a turn or a session. Put its input schema in `src/shared/`, and check it with Zod. Post the annotation to Phoenix from a new dependency in `ApiDependencies` (`src/api/api.ts`), set up in `src/main.ts`. Test it with `fetch` faked, as `src/tracing/phoenix.test.ts` does.
- **Add the ratings, the note box, and the links to the chat page.**
- **Start the session's thumbs with the user's last rating of it,** and the note box with its note, read from Phoenix when the chat opens. Added on 2026-10-26, in chat, so a session rated earlier doesn't show blank thumbs that would overwrite its rating. Turns stay as settled: replies loaded from history get no thumbs.
- **Write it down,** in functional spec 10.1, and systems design sections 4 and 10.
- **Check it locally,** with the tunnel up. Sign in as Claude Code's own user (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5). Send a chat turn to `npm run dev` through `/api`. Rate the turn at once, before its span is sent, and rate the session. Read the annotations back with Phoenix's REST API. Check each link's ID by asking Phoenix's GraphQL API the same question its redirect page asks (`getSpanByOtelId`, `getProjectSessionById`), and checking it gives the turn's trace and the chat's session. Then, in Chrome through Claude in Chrome, rate a reply and the session from the page, and open both links.

## Done when

- `npm run check` passes.
- Locally, with the tunnel up, a thumbs up with a note on a turn, sent through `/api` right after the turn ends, shows on that turn's span in Phoenix's `road-trip-agent-local` project, with its label and note. A thumbs down on the session shows on the session.
- Phoenix's GraphQL API finds the turn's trace from the span ID in its link, and the chat's session from the agent session ID in the session link.
- From the page in Chrome, a rating on a reply and on the session shows in Phoenix, and both links open the right trace and session.
- Reopening a rated session in Chrome shows its rating chosen, and its note in the note box.
- In the PR review, Joe rates a reply and the session from the page, and opens both links.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

## Why

Joe tests the coordinator by hand as it's built. Rating a turn, or a whole chat, with a note, right when it happens, records what went well and what went wrong while it's fresh. Later, the ratings get sorted into kinds of failure. The kinds that keep coming back become agent evaluations (#53). Phoenix can also turn rated spans into a dataset, which is what its experiments run on.

Phoenix's own UI can already rate a trace, but that means finding the turn in Phoenix later. From the chat, it's one click. Links from the chat to each turn's trace, and to the session, let Joe go from what he sees in the chat to how the coordinator got there. They take the place of the raw view, which #141 removes.

An **annotation** is a rating that Phoenix keeps on a span or a session: a name, a label, a score, a note, and who made it. A **session** in Phoenix groups a chat's turns by their `session.id`. That's the **agent session ID**, the Agent SDK's ID for the conversation (`agentSessionId` in `src/persistence/session.ts`), not the app's own session ID, which the page uses (systems design section 10).

## Design

Through the tunnel, Phoenix's own API docs are at `http://127.0.0.1:6006/docs`.

Agreed in chat on 2026-10-26:

- **Each reply gets a thumbs up and a thumbs down, and so does the whole session.** Either one opens a box for a note. Good turns get rated as well as bad ones.
- **Each reply gets a "View trace" link, and the chat gets a "View session" link.** Each opens Phoenix in a new tab. Phoenix 20.26 has redirect links that take our own IDs, so the app doesn't look anything up in Phoenix. `/redirects/spans/<span ID>` opens the trace with that span picked, so a turn's link needs only its turn span's ID. `/redirects/sessions/<session ID>` opens the session, and takes the agent session ID.
- **The browser never talks to Phoenix.** On the server, the browser can't reach it. So the page sends a rating to the app, under `/api`, and the app posts it to Phoenix, the way it sends traces. It posts with `fetch`, like the health check in `src/tracing/phoenix.ts`, not with a new package.
- **The links work only on Joe's machine, with the SSH tunnel up** (DEVELOPMENT.md section 2), since Phoenix's UI is at `http://127.0.0.1:6006` there and nowhere else.

What Phoenix 20.26 offers, from its source:

- `POST /v1/span_annotations` and `POST /v1/session_annotations` save annotations. Each one has a `name`, an `annotator_kind` of `HUMAN`, `CODE`, or `LLM`, a `result` with a `label`, a `score`, and an `explanation`, `metadata`, and an `identifier`.
- When an annotation with the same name and `identifier` is already there, Phoenix updates it in place of adding one.
- By default, Phoenix queues an annotation and replies at once. With `?sync=true`, it saves it before replying, and refuses one for a span it doesn't have, with a 404.
